phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Abstract interpretation analysis of EIP-7702 authorization replay protection mechanism focusing on nonce validation and increment operations. Since Prysm is a consensus layer client, this analysis examines the theoretical execution layer implementation that would be validated by the consensus client.

code_scope.context: EIP-7702 introduces a new transaction type (0x04) that allows EOAs to temporarily delegate their code execution to a smart contract. The authorization tuple includes (chain_id, address, nonce, y_parity, r, s). This analysis focuses on the nonce handling mechanism that prevents replay attacks.
code_scope.note: Prysm is a consensus client and does not directly implement EIP-7702 logic. This analysis models the expected behavior that execution clients must implement.

authorizer_nonce.description: Account nonce of the authorizing account
authorizer_nonce.monotonicity: Strictly increasing (non-decreasing) under successful authorization processing

authorization_nonce.description: Nonce value embedded in the authorization tuple

authorization_validity.description: Result of authorization validation including nonce check

states: S1: Authorization validated (nonce = N, auth pending)
transitions: S1 → S2: apply authorization AND increment nonce
S1 → S_reject: if any validation fails

replay_window.description: Time window in which an authorization could be replayed
replay_window.analysis: If nonce is NOT incremented after successful authorization, Window = infinite (replay always possible)

nonce_validation_transform.analysis: This is a deterministic equality check. If M ≠ N, authorization MUST be rejected.

nonce_increment_transform.analysis: CRITICAL: This transformation MUST occur atomically with authorization application. If this step is omitted, skipped, or fails, replay attacks become possible.

overflow_behavior.analysis: Nonce overflow is theoretically possible but practically infeasible (requires 2^64 authorizations from a single account). However, implementations must handle this case deterministically.

state_anomalies_found.title: Authorization Processed Without Nonce Increment
state_anomalies_found.description: If the code path applies the authorization (sets delegated code) but fails to increment the authorizer's nonce, the same authorization can be replayed indefinitely.
state_anomalies_found.consequence: Replay Attack - The authorization can be reused in subsequent transactions, allowing unauthorized re-delegation of the account's code execution authority.

attack_vector.step1: Attacker obtains a valid authorization from victim (nonce=N)
attack_vector.step2: Transaction T1 processes authorization, but nonce remains N
attack_vector.step3: Attacker submits Transaction T2 with same authorization
attack_vector.step4: Since nonce is still N, authorization passes validation again
attack_vector.step5: Unlimited replay possible until nonce changes

mitigations: Ensure nonce increment is tightly coupled with authorization application
Add assertion: post(nonce) = pre(nonce) + 1 after each successful authorization

state_anomalies_found.title: Same Authorization Accepted Twice in Race Window
state_anomalies_found.description: If two transactions containing the same authorization are processed concurrently (e.g., in different blocks during a reorg, or in parallel validation), both might read nonce=N, validate successfully, and apply the authorization before nonce is incremented.
state_anomalies_found.abstract_condition: ∃ T1, T2: (T1.auth == T2.auth) ∧ (read_nonce(T1) == read_nonce(T2) == N) ∧ (both_validated == true)
state_anomalies_found.consequence: Double-processing of authorization in race window before state synchronization

attack_vector.step1: Attacker crafts two transactions T1 and T2 with same authorization (nonce=N)
attack_vector.step2: T1 and T2 are submitted to different nodes or blocks
attack_vector.step3: Both transactions read authorizer.nonce = N concurrently
attack_vector.step5: If nonce increment is not atomic with authorization check, both might apply

mitigations: Enforce sequential transaction processing per account
Use atomic read-modify-write for nonce operations
Implement proper state locking during authorization processing
Ensure block-level determinism: only one transaction can consume a given nonce

state_anomalies_found.title: Nonce Incremented for Invalid Authorization
state_anomalies_found.description: If nonce is incremented even when authorization validation fails (e.g., invalid signature, wrong chain_id), this could be exploited for nonce exhaustion DoS.
state_anomalies_found.consequence: Nonce exhaustion attack - attacker forces victim's nonce to increment without valid authorization, potentially breaking expected nonce sequences

attack_vector.step1: Attacker crafts invalid authorizations for victim account
attack_vector.step2: If implementation incorrectly increments nonce on validation failure
attack_vector.step3: Attacker can force nonce to increment arbitrarily
attack_vector.step4: Victim's future authorizations become invalid due to nonce mismatch

mitigations: Only increment nonce after ALL validations pass
Nonce increment MUST be in same atomic transaction as authorization application
Add precondition: authorization_valid == true BEFORE nonce increment

state_anomalies_found.title: Undefined Behavior at Nonce = 2^64-1
state_anomalies_found.description: When authorizer nonce reaches maximum value (2^64-1), increment operation may overflow to 0 or cause undefined behavior depending on implementation.
state_anomalies_found.consequence: Nonce wraps to 0, potentially enabling replay of old authorizations that were signed with nonce=0
mitigations: Consider rejecting authorizations when nonce = 2^64-1 (though practically unnecessary)
Ensure all implementations handle overflow identically for consensus

state_anomalies_found.title: Authorization Applied but Nonce Increment Reverted
state_anomalies_found.description: If the transaction applies authorization and increments nonce, but then reverts due to out-of-gas or other failure, the authorization state change must also revert. Inconsistent revert behavior could leave authorization applied with old nonce.
state_anomalies_found.abstract_condition: authorization_applied == true ∧ nonce_incremented == true ∧ transaction_reverted == true ∧ (post(code) != pre(code) ∨ post(nonce) != pre(nonce))
state_anomalies_found.consequence: State inconsistency - authorization persists but nonce didn't increment, enabling replay

attack_vector.step1: Attacker crafts transaction that applies authorization then runs out of gas
attack_vector.step2: If state revert is incomplete, authorization might persist

mitigations: Ensure authorization processing is part of transaction's atomic state changes
All state changes (code, nonce) must revert together on transaction failure

state_anomalies_found.type: Multiple Authorizations for Same Account in Single Transaction
state_anomalies_found.title: Nonce Increment Semantics for Duplicate Authorizer
state_anomalies_found.description: If a transaction contains multiple authorizations for the same authorizer address, the nonce increment semantics must be well-defined. Should nonce increment once or multiple times?
state_anomalies_found.consequence: Non-deterministic nonce state if implementations disagree on increment count
state_anomalies_found.analysis: According to PROP-W6B15-7, 'last valid authorization wins'. This suggests nonce should increment only ONCE per unique authorizer, regardless of how many authorizations target that address.
state_anomalies_found.expected_behavior: For transaction with [Auth1(A→X, nonce=N), Auth2(A→Y, nonce=N)]: validate both against nonce=N, apply last valid one, increment nonce to N+1 once.
mitigations: Clearly specify: nonce increments once per unique authorizer per transaction
Process authorizations in order, last valid one wins
Single nonce increment after all authorizations for same address processed

normal_path: 2. Extract authorizer address from authorization (via ecrecover or direct field)
5. If invalid: reject authorization, continue to next
7. If all valid: apply code delegation
vulnerable_path_1: 8. OMITTED: Nonce increment missing or conditional on wrong criteria
9. Authorization applied but nonce unchanged → REPLAY POSSIBLE
vulnerable_path_2: 4. Nonce validation SKIPPED or always returns true

static_analysis: Trace all code paths from authorization validation to nonce increment
Verify nonce increment is unreachable from validation failure paths
Check for conditional nonce increments based on wrong predicates
Verify no early returns between authorization application and nonce increment
symbolic_execution: Symbolically execute with auth.nonce = N, account.nonce = N
Assert: if authorization applies, final account.nonce = N+1
Test with auth.nonce = N-1: authorization must be rejected
Test with auth.nonce = N+1: authorization must be rejected
invariant_checking: Post-state: if M == N and all validations pass: account.nonce = N+1
Post-state: if M != N or any validation fails: account.nonce = N (unchanged)

test_vectors.scenario: Two identical authorizations in same transaction

expected_output.reason: After first auth, nonce becomes N+1, second auth with nonce=N fails validation

test_vectors.scenario: Two different transactions with same authorization

consensus_layer_implications.note: Since Prysm is a consensus layer client, it does not execute EIP-7702 logic directly. However, it must validate execution payloads from the execution client.
validation_responsibilities: Verify execution payload state_root matches the post-state after authorization processing
Ensure execution client correctly reports gas usage including authorization processing costs
Validate that block is valid according to execution layer rules (including EIP-7702)
consensus_layer_implications.trust_boundary: Consensus client trusts execution client to correctly implement EIP-7702 nonce handling. Incorrect implementation in EL would manifest as consensus divergence if different EL clients behave differently.
consensus_layer_implications.bug_bounty_relevance: If multiple execution clients implement nonce increment differently, consensus divergence would occur, which is in-scope for bug bounties.

related_anomalies.nonce_validation_bypass: If authorization.nonce validation is skipped entirely (PROP-W6B15-5), replay is possible even with correct nonce increment
related_anomalies.signature_malleability: If signature validation allows malleable signatures (PROP-W6B15-2), attacker might replay authorization with different signature but same nonce
related_anomalies.chain_id_replay: If chain_id validation is missing (PROP-W6B15-4), authorization from one chain can replay on another, independent of nonce

anti_patterns.risk: If functions are called independently, nonce might not increment
Nonce might not increment on all success paths
Nonce increments even for invalid authorizations

key_findings: The nonce variable has a strict monotonicity property: it must increase by exactly 1 for each successful authorization
Any deviation from this monotonicity (no increment, double increment, conditional increment) creates replay attack surface
The nonce increment must be atomic with authorization application to prevent race conditions
State revert handling must ensure both authorization and nonce changes revert together
verification_required: Static analysis to confirm nonce increment is on all success paths
Dynamic analysis to test replay scenarios
Fuzz testing with multiple authorizations per transaction
Cross-client comparison to ensure deterministic nonce handling
next_phase_recommendations: Phase 2 (Symbolic Execution): Symbolically trace nonce variable through all code paths to prove increment always occurs
Phase 3 (Invariant Proving): Formally prove the nonce monotonicity invariant holds for all execution traces
Reachability Analysis: Confirm authorization processing code is reachable from transaction validation entry points
